newsitem.title: GERMANY: Lebed says he wants to cooperate with Germany.
newsitem.headline: Lebed says he wants to cooperate with Germany.

text.p: Would-be Russian presidential candidate Alexander Lebed said on Wednesday at the start of a five-day visit that he hoped he and Germany would be able to do business with each other.

The gruff retired general, on only his third visit outside the former Soviet Union, has come to Russia's biggest creditor and supporter in the West with the aim of introducing himself to the establishment as a potential successor to Boris Yeltsin.

"Germany must look at me, I need to look at Germany, we have to decide whether we should work together or not. I hope that we come to the conclusion that we should work together," Lebed told Reuters Television in an interview.

Lebed, who came a strong third in a presidential election last June and briefly served as Yeltsin's security adviser, has not concealed the fact that he believes Yeltsin should quit because of his continuing ill health and allow a new election.

But on Wednesday, before a two-hour closed-door meeting with a group of German political and economic experts, he was moderating his strident tones and stressing his respect for the electoral process.

"The Russian people made their choice last year, the president was elected. Now he's become rather ill. We all hope he recovers. I'm gearing up for a long-term task, tough and exhausting work. It won't be a simple or easy process."

Lebed admits he is conscious of the close personal relationship linking Yeltsin and Chancellor Helmut Kohl, Russia's leading advocate in its attempts to become integrated in Western economic and political structures.

He said he well understood why Kohl or President Roman Herzog had not asked to meet him, although he is due to meet the heads of all the main parliamentary parties, including Kohl's powerful lieutenant Wolfgang Schaeuble.

"The official figures here have close ties to official figures in Russia, I don't really fit into that system," he said. "It would have been tactless for them to invite me or for me to try to insist. The time isn't right now, but the time will come for us to meet."
Lebed arrived in Bonn on Tuesday and had a busy schedule of political meetings in the city for Wednesday and Thursday.
He is due to travel to Duesseldorf late on Thursday for a speech to industrialists, and on Friday will meet Bavarian state premier Edmund Stoiber in Munich.
Lebed, who visited NATO headquarters in Brussels during his spell as security adviser, has also tried to preach a spirit of cooperation with the Western alliance while emphasising Russia's interests.
He said on Wednesday it was wrong to speak of NATO's planned eastward expansion -- strongly opposed by Moscow -- as a "threat" to Russia.

"We have to ask ourselves what we want, on this little globe of ours. If we want to pander to the self-congratulation of the winners of the Cold War, that's one thing. If we want to build a system of European security, that's another thing.

"At the moment we are acting along the former lines -- 'We are big and strong and if we decide to move forward we'll move forward'. But if Russia makes up half of Europe, then no serious, solid security system can be built without Russia."
